title: Other Rooms
dimensions: 8.6 × 11.1 × 0.5 in (21.8 × 28.2 cm); 29 cm per Getty record

description.main: Jo Ann Callis's colour photographs of the nude from 1976 and 1977, the Early Color series, published in full for the first time by Aperture in 2014 with an essay by Francine Prose.
description.extended:
Other Rooms is the first book to present Jo Ann Callis's colour photographs of the nude from 1976 and 1977 in full, work she made in Los Angeles and kept largely out of view for almost forty years.

Aperture published it in 2014 as an 88-page hardcover with an essay, titled Honey, by the novelist Francine Prose. The pictures come from the series Callis provisionally called Early Color, plus black-and-white photographs from the same period. Her models pose naked in bare, anonymous rooms, often cropped to a torso, a pair of legs or a hand, and are bound or marked with household materials. Twine, belts and tape press into the skin; honey, sand and cloth are laid against it. The cover image shows a man's hand gripping the ankles of a woman standing on a dining chair. Callis arranges every scene before the camera, and the constraint in each picture reads as both a joke and a threat.

Callis was born in 1940 and began teaching at CalArts in 1976, the year this work starts. She is known for staged photographs made in the studio and at home, and the J. Paul Getty Museum gave her the retrospective Woman Twirling in 2009. The library also holds her two Nazraeli Press One Picture Books, Black Sun and Cheap Thrills.
description.artist_bio: Jo Ann Callis (born 1940) is a Los Angeles photographer who has taught at CalArts since 1976. She is known for staged colour photographs of figures, interiors and objects. The J. Paul Getty Museum presented her retrospective Woman Twirling in 2009. She has received NEA fellowships in 1980, 1985 and 1991 and a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1990. Her work is held by the Museum of Modern Art, LACMA, the Hammer Museum, MOCA Los Angeles and SFMOMA.
